newsitem.title: UK: SERIOUS FRAUD OFFICE APPOINTS NEW DIRECTOR.
newsitem.headline: SERIOUS FRAUD OFFICE APPOINTS NEW DIRECTOR.

text.p: Britain's Serious Fraud Office said on Monday it had appointed Rosalind Wright as its new director.
Wright will take over at the SFO, which leads investigations into allegations of major fraud in financial markets and the business world, on April 21.
Wright, a lawyer currently with markets regulation body the Securities and Futures Authority, succeeds George Staple.
Wright, 54, was appointed by Britain's Attorney General Sir Nicholas Lyell and becomes the fourth director of the SFO, which was set up in 1988.

Staple will return to law firm Clifford Chance, where he is a partner, when he leaves the SFO after completing his five-year term. Last year he questioned if a jury was the right body to decide verdicts in lengthy and complicated fraud trials.

His comments came after a high-profile ruling in the trial of Kevin Maxwell, son of media tycoon Robert Maxwell who died in 1991. Kevin's second trial, which followed his acquittal at a previous trial, was thrown out and a not guilty verdict given.

The SFO has been criticised for not securing convictions in several high-profile cases but has defended its record. It said it had achieved an overall conviction rate of around 63 percent, with more than three out of four cases ending in at least one conviction.
